etapes: Start the rice. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and set them aside in a bowl of warm water: they will hold together better while cooking.
Chop the garlic, the ginger and the white part of the spring onions. Keep the green for the end.
Fry the minced pork over high heat until it colours and breaks into grains, 4 min.
Add garlic, ginger, doubanjiang and miso. Stir 1 min — the paste should turn dark red and fragrant.
Pour in 150 ml of water and the soy sauce, simmer 3 min.
Add the drained tofu, shaking the pan rather than stirring so it doesn't break up. Leave 4 min.
Slake the cornflour in a little cold water, pour it in slowly and stir until the sauce coats the spoon.
Off the heat: sesame oil, crushed Sichuan pepper, spring onion greens. Serve over the rice.
Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Blend the drained chickpeas with the onion, the garlic, half the herbs, the cumin and the ground coriander. The texture should stay coarse, not smooth.
Salt, shape a dozen flattened balls, oil them and bake 25 min, turning them halfway.
Meanwhile, pour 120 ml of boiling salted water over the couscous, cover and let it swell 10 min.
Dice the cucumber and cherry tomatoes, chop the rest of the herbs, mix it all into the couscous with the lemon juice and a drizzle of oil.
Build the bowls: tabbouleh, falafels, a spoonful of hummus and of yoghurt.
Heat the oven to 210 °C.
Cut the red kuri squash into 3 cm cubes, toss with the chickpeas — well drained and dried — the oil, the cumin and the paprika.
Bake 30 min: the chickpeas should crisp and the squash brown at the corners.
Cook the quinoa 12 min in twice its volume of salted water, then let it rest covered 5 min off the heat.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and 2 tbsp of cold water — the sauce will thicken first, then loosen again, that's normal.
Massage the kale with a pinch of salt to tenderise it, slice the radishes, slice the avocado.
Assemble and spoon over the tahini sauce.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Prick the sweet potatoes with a fork and bake them whole 45 min, until a knife goes through without resistance.
Halfway through, add the chickpeas to the tray, drained, oiled and tossed with the spices.
Whisk the yoghurt with the tahini and the lemon juice.
Split the potatoes lengthways, mash the flesh a little with a fork.
Top with the spiced chickpeas, spoon over the sauce, scatter with spring onion and sliced chilli.
Slice the onion, chop the garlic, the ginger and the chilli.
Fry the onion 5 min over medium heat until it turns translucent.
Add garlic, ginger, chilli and every spice except the garam masala. Stir 1 min — the spices should perfume without burning.
Pour in the rinsed lentils, the tomatoes, the coconut milk and 200 ml of water.
Simmer 20 min covered, stirring now and then. The lentils should collapse completely.
Off the heat: garam masala, salt, lemon juice and chopped coriander.
Start the rice.
Fry the sliced onion 5 min, then add garlic, ginger and the spices except the garam masala.
Pour in the tomatoes and the coconut milk, reduce 10 min uncovered until the sauce thickens.
Add the drained chickpeas, leave 5 min more.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time: it wilts in seconds.
Finish with the garam masala, the lime juice and the coriander.
Cut the chicken into strips, toss with the spices, the paprika, the oil and the juice of one lime. Marinate 10 min.
Meanwhile, make the pico de gallo: cherry tomatoes quartered, half the red onion finely diced, coriander, lime juice.
Mash the avocado with a fork, with salt and a little lemon juice.
Mix the cream and the sriracha.
Sear the chicken over high heat 6 min, without stirring constantly so it colours.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds in a dry pan, then fill them.
Cook the noodles as the packet says, rinse them under cold water and set aside.
Break the broccoli into small florets and cut the carrots into thin batons.
Heat a wok over high heat, sear garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Add carrots and broccoli, stir-fry 5 min: the vegetables should stay crunchy and catch a little colour.
Add the drained chickpeas, the noodles, the soy sauce and the lao gan ma. Stir-fry 2 min, tossing.
Off the heat, pour in the sesame oil.
The rice must be cold, ideally cooked the day before: warm, it clumps and won't fry.
Cut the carrot into small dice, chop the garlic, slice the spring onions.
Stir-fry carrot and garlic 3 min over high heat.
Add the rice, press it a little with the spatula to separate the grains, fry 4 min without stirring too much.
Push the rice to one side, break the eggs into the free space, scramble them then fold everything together.
Finish with the soy sauce, the sesame oil and the spring onion greens.
Break the cauliflower into florets and cook them 10 min in boiling salted water: a knife should go in easily but the floret should stay whole.
Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Brown the bacon lardons in a dry pan 4 min.
Drain the cauliflower very thoroughly — leftover water is what makes a gratin bland.
Lay the cauliflower in a dish with the ham cut into strips and the lardons. Pour over the hot milk, salt and pepper.
Cover with grated cheese and bake 25 min, until the top is well coloured.
Break the cauliflower into florets and cook them 12 min in boiling salted water.
Heat the milk without letting it boil.
Drain the cauliflower, blend it with the hot milk until smooth.
Salt and pepper generously. It's creamy without a drop of cream.
Cut the bell pepper and carrot into very thin batons, cut the ham into strips.
Soak a sheet of rice paper 30 seconds in warm water: it should stay slightly firm, it will finish softening on the worktop.
Fill the bottom third, fold the sides in then roll tightly.
Serve with the soy sauce. The principle works with just about anything left in the fridge.
Rinse and drain everything tinned — that's the difference between a fresh salad and a briny one.
Slice the hearts of palm into rounds.
Flake the tuna coarsely.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice and salt, pour over everything and fold gently.
Rest 10 min in the fridge before serving.
Start the pasta in a big pan of well-salted water.
Fry the crushed garlic 30 seconds in the oil, then pour in the tomatoes. Reduce 10 min.
Add chickpeas, peas and olives, warm through 3 min.
Stir in the drained tuna and the cream off the heat, so the tuna doesn't dry out.
Drain the pasta keeping a ladle of cooking water, fold together and loosen the sauce if needed.
Fry the sliced onion and the garlic 5 min in a large sauté pan.
Add the tomatoes and 700 ml of salted water, bring to the boil.
Tip the dry pasta straight in and cook uncovered for the time on the packet, stirring regularly.
Two minutes before the end, add the drained chickpeas, flageolet beans, sweetcorn and peas.
Off the heat: tuna, olives and cream. The sauce should coat the pasta without being runny.
If it's too thick, a little hot water; too runny, two more minutes over high heat.
Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil and cook the pasta in it.
Meanwhile, grate the parmesan and zest the lemon.
Mix the cream, the parmesan, the zest and the crushed garlic in a bowl.
Drain the pasta keeping a ladle of cooking water.
Tip the piping-hot pasta onto the mixture, add a little cooking water and stir briskly until the sauce coats.
Pepper generously and serve at once.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the short pasta as the packet says, until it stays firm to the bite.
Drain and rinse immediately under cold water to stop the cooking and stop it clumping as it cools.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber small, and slice the red onion finely.
Chop the basil, drain the black olives and tear the mozzarella into small pieces.
In a big bowl, mix the cooled pasta, the vegetables, the mozzarella, the basil and the olives.
Whisk the olive oil with the balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper, pour over the salad and toss.
Rest 10 min in the fridge before serving, long enough for the flavours to come together.
Cook the sushi rice as the packet says, then season it while still hot with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Let it cool to lukewarm.
Cut the fresh salmon into 1.5 cm cubes.
Marinate the salmon 10 min with the soy sauce, the sesame oil and the lime juice — no longer, or the acid starts to cook the fish.
Slice the avocado and the cucumber, thinly slice the radishes.
Divide the warm rice between the bowls, then arrange salmon, avocado, cucumber, radish and edamame.
Scatter with sesame seeds and spoon over the rest of the marinade before serving.
Start the white rice.
Slice the onion, chop the garlic and the fresh chilli, dice the bell peppers.
Fry the onion and the peppers 5 min in the olive oil until they soften.
Add the garlic, the chilli, the ground cumin, the smoked paprika and the mexican spice mix. Stir 1 min, long enough for it to smell good.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes, the drained kidney beans and chickpeas, the sweetcorn and 100 ml of water.
Simmer 20 min uncovered, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
Salt and serve over the rice.
Start the white rice.
Cut the chicken breast into pieces, the aubergine into cubes and the bell pepper into strips.
Heat the olive oil in a wok, fry the green curry paste 1 min over medium heat until it smells fragrant.
Add the chicken, sear 4 min over high heat until it turns white all over.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the aubergine and the pepper. Simmer 15 min covered, until the aubergine is meltingly soft.
Season with the fish sauce and the brown sugar, taste and adjust.
Off the heat, add the lime juice and the chopped fresh basil. Serve over the rice.
Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Cut the aubergine, the courgettes, the bell peppers and the tomatoes into even pieces of about 2 cm.
Slice the onion and the garlic.
Toss all the vegetables in a large dish with the olive oil, the herbes de Provence, salt and pepper.
Bake 40 min, stirring halfway, until the vegetables are soft and lightly caramelised at the edges.
In the last 5 minutes, hollow out four wells in the vegetables and break the eggs into them. Return to the oven until the white is set and the yolk still runny.
Serve straight from the dish.
Heat the oven to 190 °C.
Unroll the shortcrust pastry into a tart tin and prick it with a fork.
Slice the courgettes thinly, sweat them 5 min in a pan so they stop releasing water inside the quiche.
Whisk the eggs with the crème fraîche, the milk, salt, pepper and the nutmeg.
Spread the courgettes over the pastry base, pour in the custard, cover with rounds of goat cheese log.
Bake 30 min, until the quiche is golden and barely wobbling in the middle.
Peel and cut the carrots into chunks, the courgettes into thick batons, slice the onions.
Brown the chicken thighs in the olive oil 5 min on all sides.
Add the onions, the ground cumin and the harissa, stir 1 min.
Add the carrots and 800 ml of water, salt, cover and simmer 20 min.
Add the courgettes and the drained chickpeas, carry on cooking 15 min.
Meanwhile, prepare the fine couscous with the raisins as the packet says.
Serve the chicken and vegetables over the couscous, moistened with a little broth.
Dissolve the stock cube in 1 l of hot water, keep it warm.
Slice the onion and the garlic, slice the button mushrooms.
Fry the mushrooms in the olive oil 5 min, set aside.
In the same pan, sweat the onion and the garlic 2 min, add the risotto rice and toast 1 min until the grains turn pearly.
Pour in the white wine, let it reduce, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring until each is absorbed, for 18 min.
Return the mushrooms, add the butter and the parmesan, pepper and serve at once.
Start the white rice.
Cut the bell peppers into strips, slice the onions and the garlic.
Brown the chicken thighs in the olive oil 8 min on all sides, set aside.
Fry the peppers and onions 5 min in the same pan.
Add the garlic, the Espelette pepper, the chopped tomatoes and the chicken, salt.
Cover and simmer 25 min over low heat. Serve over the rice.
Heat 600 ml of water without letting it boil.
Rehydrate the wakame seaweed 5 min in a bowl of cold water, drain.
Cut the silken tofu into small dice, slice the spring onion.
Slake the miso paste in a ladle of hot water then stir it back into the pan off the heat.
Add the tofu, the seaweed and the soy sauce, ladle into bowls and scatter with spring onion.
Slice the tomato and the red onion into rounds, wash the green salad.
Salt the beef patties and cook them in the olive oil 3 min a side, adding the cheddar at the end so it melts.
Toast the burger buns lightly.
Spread with ketchup and mustard, top with salad, tomato, onion and gherkins.
Lay the cheesy patty on and close the bun.
Heat the oven to 240 °C, as hot as it goes.
Roll the pizza dough out on a tray, spread with salted chopped tomatoes.
Scatter over the mozzarella, drained and torn into pieces.
Bake 12 to 15 min until the edges are golden.
Straight out of the oven, drizzle with olive oil and scatter with fresh basil.
Cook the potatoes 20 min in boiling water, until a knife goes in easily, then peel and slice them into rounds.
Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Fry the bacon lardons and the sliced onion 5 min in a dry pan.
In a dish, layer potatoes, bacon and onion, and crème fraîche, and pepper.
Cut the reblochon in half through its thickness, lay it on top rind up.
Bake 25 min until the cheese is melted and golden.
Slice the onion, the garlic and the bell pepper.
Fry the onion and the pepper 5 min in the olive oil.
Add the garlic, the ground cumin and the smoked paprika, stir 1 min.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes, salt and simmer 10 min until it thickens.
Hollow out 4 wells in the sauce, break the eggs into them, cover and cook 6 min until the whites are set.
Scatter with fresh coriander and serve straight from the pan.
Slice the chinese cabbage very finely, salt it and let it drain 10 min then squeeze out the water.
Mix the minced pork, the cabbage, the sliced spring onion, the grated fresh ginger and garlic, the soy sauce and the sesame oil.
Put a spoonful of filling in the middle of each gyoza wrapper, wet the edges and pleat to seal.
Brown the gyoza 2 min flat side down in an oiled pan.
Pour in 60 ml of water, cover at once and steam 5 min until it has all evaporated.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cook the quinoa as the packet says.
Cut the firm tofu into cubes, coat with cornflour and olive oil.
Bake the tofu and the broccoli florets 20 min, until the tofu is golden and crisp.
Grate the carrots, slice the avocado.
Divide quinoa, tofu, broccoli, carrot and avocado between the bowls, drizzle with soy sauce and scatter with sesame seeds.
Start the white rice.
Steam the broccoli 8 min.
Brown the salmon 3 min skin side down in the sesame oil, turn for 2 min.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce, reduce 2 min while spooning it over the fish.
Serve over the rice with the broccoli, scattered with sesame seeds.
Cut the lamb shoulder into large cubes, slice the onions and the garlic.
Brown the meat in the olive oil 8 min on all sides, set aside.
Fry the onion and the garlic 5 min, add the cinnamon and the ground cumin.
Return the meat, cover with water, salt, cover and simmer 1 h over low heat.
Add the dried apricots and carry on 15 min.
Prepare the fine couscous as the packet says, scatter the tagine with flaked almonds and serve over the couscous.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water 10 min as the packet says, drain.
Cut the chicken breast into strips, chop the garlic.
Stir-fry the chicken and the garlic 5 min in a very hot wok.
Push to one side, break in the eggs and scramble 1 min, then fold into the chicken.
Add the noodles, the fish sauce and the brown sugar, stir-fry 2 min.
Add the bean sprouts, stir-fry 1 min, serve with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.
Dice the courgette and the aubergine, slice the onion and the garlic.
Fry the onion and the garlic in the olive oil 3 min, add courgette and aubergine, cook 10 min.
Add the chopped tomatoes, salt, simmer 10 min.
Make a béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour, cook 1 min then pour in the milk little by little, whisking, until it thickens.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Layer in a dish: tomato and vegetable sauce, lasagne sheets, béchamel, three times over.
Finish with the béchamel, the mozzarella and the parmesan. Bake 30 min until the top is browned.
Cut the meat into large 4 cm cubes and pat them dry: a wet surface doesn't colour, it boils.
Sear the cubes in two batches in a very hot casserole, 5 min a batch, until deep brown all over. Set aside.
Render the bacon lardons with the sliced onions and the carrots in thick rounds in the same casserole, 8 min.
Return the meat, dust with flour, stir and leave 2 min: that is what will thicken the sauce.
Add the crushed garlic, the tomato purée, the bouquet garni, pour in the red wine and top up with water and the stock to cover.
Cover and simmer at the barest bubble for 3 h. The meat is ready when a fork goes in without resistance.
Fry the mushrooms separately 5 min over high heat and add them in the last ten minutes, otherwise they release their water into the sauce.
Taste, salt, pepper. Better reheated the next day.
Put the veal in a casserole, cover with cold water, bring to a bare simmer and skim off the grey foam for 5 min: that is what keeps the broth clear.
Add the carrots in chunks, the leeks, the onion and the bouquet garni. Cook covered 1 h, never at a hard boil.
Lift out the meat and vegetables, strain the broth and keep 75 cl of it.
Make a white roux: melt the butter, add the flour, stir 2 min without letting it colour.
Pour in the hot broth little by little, whisking, and let it thicken 10 min.
Cook the sliced mushrooms 5 min in a little broth with a squeeze of lemon.
Off the heat, slake the egg yolk in the cream and stir it into the sauce — it must not boil after that, or it will split.
Return meat, vegetables and mushrooms to the sauce, reheat gently and serve with the rice.
Salt and pepper the thighs, brown them skin side down 8 min in the casserole, then 4 min on the other side. Set aside.
Pour off half the fat, sweat the sliced onions, the carrots in rounds and the bacon lardons 8 min.
Dust with flour, stir 2 min, add the garlic and the tomato purée.
Return the chicken, pour in the red wine, add the bouquet garni. The liquid should just come up to the meat.
Cover and simmer 1 h over low heat.
Fry the mushrooms in butter 5 min separately and add them at the end.
Lift out the chicken, reduce the sauce uncovered 10 min if it is too thin, then check the seasoning.
Put the meat in a large stockpot, cover generously with cold water and bring gently to a simmer.
Skim carefully for 10 min, until the surface stays clean.
Add the studded onion, the garlic, the bouquet garni and the celery. Salt. Cook covered 2 h at the barest bubble.
Add carrots, turnips and leeks tied in a bundle, carry on 45 min.
Cook the potatoes separately in a ladle of broth 25 min: in the pot they would cloud it.
Serve the meat sliced and surrounded by its vegetables, with mustard and gherkins. The broth is drunk first, in a bowl.
Cut the lamb into 5 cm pieces, sear them over high heat in the casserole 6 min until well coloured.
Dust with sugar and let it caramelise 1 min: that is what gives a navarin its colour.
Add the flour, stir, then the garlic, the tomato purée and the stock dissolved in 50 cl of hot water.
Add the bouquet garni, cover and simmer 45 min.
Add carrots, turnips and potatoes cut into large pieces, carry on 30 min uncovered.
Throw in the peas 5 min before the end. Check salt and pepper.
The day before if you can: marinate the cubed meat with the wine, the carrots in rounds, the onions and the bouquet garni, in the fridge.
Drain the meat keeping the marinade, pat it dry and brown it in two batches, 5 min a batch.
Add the drained vegetables, fry 8 min, dust with flour.
Pour in the strained marinade, the chopped tomatoes, the crushed garlic and a wide ribbon of orange zest.
Cover and simmer 3 h over very low heat — a barely visible tremble.
Add the olives in the last quarter of an hour. Serve with short pasta or steamed potatoes.
Soak the beans the day before, then cook them 45 min in simmering water with the smoked pork belly, the onion, the carrot and the bouquet garni.
Brown the sausages 8 min in a pan, set aside. Warm the duck legs 5 min to shed their set fat.
Fry the second onion and the chopped garlic in a spoonful of duck fat, add the tomatoes and the purée, leave 10 min.
Fold the drained beans into that sauce, moisten with 50 cl of their cooking water and the stock.
In a deep oven dish, layer beans, pieces of meat and beans. The liquid should just come up without drowning it.
Bake 1 h at 150 °C. Break the crust with a spoon three or four times during cooking: that is what thickens it.
Rinse the sauerkraut under cold water and squeeze it hard between your hands: that is what sets its acidity.
Sweat the sliced onions in a casserole 5 min, without colouring them.
Add half the sauerkraut, lay the smoked pork belly and the roast on top, cover with the rest of the sauerkraut.
Pour in the white wine and 25 cl of water, add the juniper berries and the bouquet garni. Cover.
Cook 1 h over low heat. Add the sausages and the peeled potatoes, carry on 30 min.
Serve from the dish, meats sliced on top, mustard on the side.
Blanch the smoked pork belly 10 min in boiling water to draw out the salt, then cut it into thick lardons.
Fry the onion, the shallots and the carrots in rounds 6 min in the casserole.
Add the rinsed lentils, the pork belly, the garlic, the bouquet garni and cover with 1.2 l of cold water. Don't salt yet: salt toughens the skin of the lentils.
Bring to a simmer and cook 30 min covered.
Add the sausages, pricked with a fork, carry on 15 min.
Salt at the end, pepper, and serve with the mustard.
Cut the meat into cubes, brown it in small batches 5 min a batch in the casserole.
Set the meat aside, fry the sliced onions 6 min in the pan juices.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping the bottom with a wooden spoon: all the flavour is there.
Return the meat, add the carrots in thick chunks, the garlic, the purée, the bouquet garni and the stock with 30 cl of water.
Cover and simmer 2 h over very low heat. The carrots should be on the point of falling apart.
Uncover for the last 15 min to reduce the sauce, then check the seasoning.
Brown the seasoned thighs 10 min on both sides in a sauté pan. Set aside.
Sweat the chopped shallots 3 min, add the sliced mushrooms and turn the heat up 6 min to drive off their water.
Dust with flour, deglaze with white wine, reduce 3 min.
Add the chopped tomatoes, the garlic and the tarragon, return the chicken and simmer 30 min covered.
Add the cream, leave 5 min uncovered, then scatter with parsley.
Coat the rabbit pieces generously with mustard and leave them 15 min at room temperature.
Flour them lightly and brown them 8 min in butter and oil in a casserole, gently: mustard burns fast.
Add the sliced shallots, leave 3 min.
Deglaze with white wine, add the thyme, cover and simmer 35 min.
Lift out the pieces, pour the cream into the casserole and reduce 5 min over high heat.
Return the rabbit to the sauce, pepper generously and serve with fresh pasta.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Take the chicken out of the fridge 20 min ahead: a chilled bird cooks dry on the outside before it is done at the centre.
Slide the soft butter under the skin of the breasts, salt and pepper all over, inside too.
Shut the lemon, pricked with a fork, two garlic cloves and the thyme into the cavity.
Lay the chicken on its side in a large dish, surrounded by the potatoes in wedges, the garlic in its skin and the oil.
Roast 25 min, turn onto the other side for 25 min, then finish 25 min on its back to colour the breast.
Check by piercing the thigh: the juices should run clear. Rest 10 min before carving, or the juices run into the dish.
Cook the peeled potatoes 25 min in salted water, until a knife goes through without effort.
Meanwhile, fry the chopped onions 6 min, add the meat and press it with a spoon so it cooks in grains, 8 min.
Add the garlic, the chopped tomatoes, the parsley, salt and pepper. Leave 10 min uncovered: the filling should be moist, never runny.
Mash the potatoes, beat in the hot milk, the butter and the nutmeg. Don't blend, the mash would turn elastic.
Spread the meat in a dish, cover with mash, score with a fork and scatter with grated cheese.
Bake 25 min at 200 °C, until the ridges are golden.
Cut a lid off the tomatoes, hollow them out with a teaspoon keeping the pulp. Salt the inside and turn them upside down for 10 min to drain.
Soak the sandwich bread in the milk, then squeeze it out.
Mix by hand the meat, the chopped onion and garlic, the egg, the squeezed bread, the parsley, salt and pepper.
Fill the tomatoes without packing them down, put the lids back on.
Scatter the dry rice and the chopped pulp over the bottom of the dish with a glass of water: it will cook in the tomato juices.
Bake 55 min at 180 °C. Baste once halfway through.
Start the pasta water. Flour the escalopes lightly, salt and pepper.
Sear them 3 min a side in the hot butter, then keep them warm under a sheet of foil.
In the same pan, sweat the shallots 2 min, add the sliced mushrooms and cook 6 min over high heat.
Deglaze with white wine, reduce by half, 3 min.
Pour in the cream, let it thicken 4 min, return the escalopes for a minute to warm through.
Scatter with parsley and serve over the drained pasta.
Butterfly each chicken breast and flatten it between two sheets of baking paper to 1 cm thick.
Salt, pepper, lay on a slice of ham and of comté, close it up pressing the edges well.
Pass each cordon bleu through the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs. Repeat egg and breadcrumbs on the edges: that is where the cheese escapes.
Cook the green beans 8 min in boiling salted water.
Brown the cordons bleus 5 min a side over medium heat in the oil — too fierce and the crumb burns before the chicken is cooked.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve at once.
Cut the potatoes into one-centimetre batons, rinse them under cold water then dry them thoroughly in a tea towel.
First fry: drop the chips 7 min into oil at 150 °C, they should stay pale and floppy. Drain them and let them rest.
Take the meat out of the fridge 20 min ahead, salt it just before cooking.
Sear the steaks 2 min a side in a very hot pan with the butter, basting. Rest them 5 min on a warm plate.
Second fry: 3 min at 180 °C, until golden and crisp. Salt as they come out.
Serve with the dressed salad and the mustard.
Cook the potatoes in their skins 25 min in salted water.
Sear the seasoned chops 4 min a side in the butter and oil, then keep them warm.
Sweat the chopped shallots 3 min in the pan juices, dust with flour.
Deglaze with white wine, add the stock dissolved in 15 cl of water, reduce 5 min.
Off the heat, stir in the mustard and the sliced gherkins: boiled mustard turns bitter.
Spoon the sauce over the chops and serve with the potatoes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Brush the roast with mustard, salt, pepper, scatter with thyme.
Colour it 8 min on all sides in an ovenproof casserole.
Add the potatoes in wedges, the onions in slivers and the garlic in its skin, drizzle with oil and toss.
Pour the stock dissolved in 20 cl of hot water into the bottom of the dish.
Roast 1 h, turning the potatoes halfway through.
Rest the meat 10 min under foil before slicing.
Cook the potatoes, peeled and cut into large pieces, 25 min in salted water from cold.
Prick the sausages, brown them 15 min over medium heat in a pan with a little water: the water cooks them through, the pan colours them once it has evaporated.
Melt the sliced onions 12 min over low heat in a little oil, until golden and soft.
Drain the potatoes, pass them through a ricer, beat in the butter then the hot milk little by little.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Serve the sausages on the mash, crowned with onions.
Cook the potatoes 25 min in salted water, then mash them roughly with a fork and a knob of butter.
Cut the apples into thick wedges without peeling them and slice the onion.
Fry them in butter 10 min with the brown sugar, until the apples are golden but still whole.
Prick the black pudding and lay it in a hot pan, 5 min a side over medium heat. Don't prick it further, it would empty out.
Deglaze the apples with a splash of vinegar off the heat and serve at once.
Score the skin of the duck breasts in a criss-cross without cutting into the flesh, salt.
Lay them skin down in a cold pan, turn the heat to medium and let the fat render 8 min. Pour the fat off twice along the way.
Turn and cook 4 min flesh side for pink meat. Rest 10 min under foil — the rest matters as much as the cooking.
Fry the diced potatoes 15 min in two spoonfuls of the saved duck fat, with the thyme.
In the duck pan, brown the apple wedges 6 min with the honey, then deglaze with balsamic vinegar.
Slice the duck on the diagonal and serve with the pan juices spooned over.

gigot-agneau-flageolets.titre: Leg of lamb with flageolet beans
etapes: Take the lamb out 1 h ahead. Heat the oven to 220 °C.
Stud the meat with four garlic cloves in slivers, rub with oil, salt, pepper, scatter with thyme.
Roast 15 min at 220 °C to sear, then drop to 180 °C and count 12 min per pound for pink meat.
Fry the shallots and the remaining garlic 5 min in butter, add the drained flageolet beans and the stock dissolved in 15 cl of water.
Simmer 20 min covered, then scatter with parsley.
Rest the lamb 15 min before carving, and save the juices from the dish to moisten the beans.
Sort the mussels under cold water: throw out the broken ones and any that stay open when tapped on the sink.
Cut the potatoes into chips and give them a first fry, 7 min at 150 °C.
Sweat the chopped shallots and garlic in the butter 4 min without colouring, in a large stockpot.
Pour in the white wine, bring to a hard boil 2 min to drive off the alcohol.
Tip in the mussels all at once, cover and leave 5 min over high heat, shaking the pot once: they are ready as soon as they have all opened.
Fry the chips a second time, 3 min at 180 °C, and salt them.
Pepper the mussels, scatter with parsley and serve with the cooking juices in a bowl.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Fry the sliced onion 5 min in the oil.
Add the garlic, the diced tomatoes and the herbs, let it stew down 10 min over high heat: the sauce should thicken, not swim.
Add the olives, the capers and the white wine, carry on 3 min.
Pour the sauce into a dish, lay the cod loins on top, salt and pepper, drizzle with oil.
Bake 15 min. The fish is cooked when the flesh flakes apart under a fork.
Serve with the lemon juice squeezed over at the last moment.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the courgettes and the carrots into thin ribbons: cut thick, they would stay raw.
Lay out four large sheets of baking paper. Divide the vegetables in the centre, then the sliced shallots.
Lay a salmon fillet on each bed of vegetables, salt, pepper, add two lemon slices.
Drizzle with oil and a spoonful of white wine, then close the parcels by folding the edges over twice.
Bake 15 min: the parcel should puff up, the sign that the steam is working.
Open at the table and scatter with chopped chives.
Cook the potatoes in salted water 25 min.
Pat the trout dry, salt them inside and out, then flour them lightly, tapping off the excess.
Cook them 5 min a side in 40 g of foaming butter, over medium heat. Keep warm.
Wipe the pan, melt the rest of the butter and brown the almonds in it 2 min, stirring constantly — they go from golden to burnt in seconds.
Off the heat, add the juice of a lemon and the parsley, pour over the trout and serve with the steamed potatoes.
Start the rice. Cut the salmon into large 3 cm cubes, salt and pepper.
Sweat the chopped shallots 3 min in butter in a sauté pan.
Deglaze with white wine and reduce by half, 3 min.
Add the cream and let it thicken 4 min over low heat.
Lay the salmon cubes in the sauce, cover and leave 5 min over very low heat: the salmon should stay translucent at the centre.
Off the heat, add the chives and a squeeze of lemon. Serve over the rice.
Cook the green beans 8 min in boiling salted water, then drain them and fry them 2 min in oil.
Pat the pieces of fish dry, salt and pepper them and pass them through the flour just before cooking — too early and the flour goes soggy and sticks.
Heat 40 g of butter until it foams, lay the fish in and cook 4 min without touching it.
Turn gently with a spatula, carry on 3 min, then plate up.
Discard the cooked butter, melt the rest until it smells nutty, add the lemon juice and the parsley off the heat, and spoon over at once.
Peel the prawns keeping the tails, and pull out the black vein with a knife along the back.
Chop the garlic finely and infuse it 2 min over low heat in the olive oil: over high heat it turns bitter.
Turn the heat up, tip in the prawns and sear them 2 min a side, until pink and firm.
Deglaze with white wine, leave 1 min, then add the parsley, the Espelette pepper and the salt.
Squeeze over lemon and serve immediately with the baguette for the sauce.
Slice the leeks into thin rounds and melt them 12 min covered in 20 g of butter, with two spoonfuls of water.
Pat the scallops dry one by one: the slightest moisture makes them boil instead of colour.
Sear them 90 seconds a side in a very hot pan with the rest of the butter, salt, pepper, then set aside.
Sweat the shallots in the same pan 2 min, deglaze with white wine and reduce 3 min.
Add the cream, let it thicken 3 min, return the scallops for 30 seconds to warm through.
Plate on the melted leeks and scatter with chives.
Heat the oven to 160 °C. Rub a gratin dish with a cut garlic clove, then butter it generously.
Peel the potatoes and slice them 3 mm thick. Whatever you do, don't rinse them: their starch is what binds the gratin.
Heat the milk, the cream, the remaining crushed garlic, the salt, the pepper and the nutmeg without letting it boil.
Tip the slices into that mixture and cook 10 min over low heat, stirring gently: the gratin will go in already hot and save half an hour in the oven.
Pour into the dish, level it, dot with butter.
Bake 1 h. The top should be golden and a knife tip go through without resistance. Rest 10 min before serving.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Roll the pastry into a tin, prick it with a fork and cover it with baking paper weighed down with dried pulses.
Blind bake 12 min: without this step the base stays pale and soggy under the custard.
Fry the bacon lardons 5 min in a dry pan, then drain them on kitchen paper.
Beat the eggs with the cream and the milk, salt sparingly — the lardons and the comté are salty already — pepper, grate in the nutmeg.
Remove the pulses, scatter the lardons and the grated comté over the base, pour in the custard.
Bake 35 min, until the quiche is puffed and golden. It sinks as it cools, that's normal.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, add the flour, stir 2 min, then pour in the hot milk little by little, whisking.
Let it thicken 4 min over low heat, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. It should coat the spoon.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Spread eight slices of bread with béchamel.
On four of them, lay a slice of ham and a layer of grated comté, then close with the other slices, béchamel side in.
Coat the tops with the rest of the béchamel and the remaining comté.
Bake 12 min, then 2 min under the grill so the top blisters and browns.
Beat the eggs with a fork, just enough to mix whites and yolks: over-beaten, they make a rubbery omelette.
Add the chopped herbs, salt, pepper.
Dress the salad with oil, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Foam the butter in a pan over medium heat, pour the eggs in all at once.
Draw the edges to the centre with a spatula for 2 min, until the top is still glossy and creamy.
Roll the omelette over on itself and slide it onto the plate. Serve with the salad.
Heat the oven to 180 °C and heat a pan of water for the bain-marie.
Fry the shallot and the sliced mushrooms 6 min in butter, until their water has completely gone.
Butter four ramekins, divide the mushrooms between them then a spoonful of cream.
Break an egg into each ramekin without bursting the yolk, spoon over the rest of the cream, scatter with comté, salt and pepper.
Set the ramekins in a dish, pour in hot water halfway up and bake 10 min: the white should be set, the yolk still runny.
Scatter with chives and serve with fingers of toasted baguette.
Fry the bacon lardons, the shallots and the mushrooms 8 min in butter in a sauté pan.
Dust with flour, stir, then pour in the red wine with the garlic and the bouquet garni. Reduce 20 min over medium heat, until the sauce coats the spoon.
Toast four slices of baguette and rub them with garlic.
Bring a pan of water with the vinegar to a bare simmer — never a rolling boil, it shreds the white.
Break each egg into a bowl, slide it into the water and poach 3 min, then drain it on kitchen paper.
Set an egg on each crouton, spoon over the strained sauce and pepper.
Slice the bell peppers into thin strips and the onions into half-moons.
Melt them 20 min over low heat in the oil, covered: piperade is made with patience, not high heat.
Add the garlic and the peeled diced tomatoes, the Espelette pepper, and reduce 15 min uncovered.
Grill the slices of cured ham 1 min a side in a dry pan, set them aside.
Beat the eggs, pour them into the vegetables and stir constantly 3 min over low heat: the mixture should stay soft and loose.
Serve at once, with the cured ham laid on top.
Cut out the bitter cone at the base of each chicory head with a sharp knife.
Cook them 20 min in boiling salted water with the lemon juice and the sugar, then drain and press them firmly: a waterlogged chicory drowns the gratin.
Make the béchamel with the butter, the flour and the hot milk, let it thicken 5 min, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Wrap each chicory head in a slice of ham and lay them side by side in a buttered dish.
Coat with béchamel, scatter with grated cheese.
Bake 25 min at 200 °C, until the top is well browned.
Cook the rice 10 min in boiling salted water, drain it: it will finish cooking in the gratin.
Coarsely grate the courgettes, salt them and let them drain 10 min in a colander, then squeeze them out by the handful.
Fry the chopped onion and garlic 5 min, add the courgettes and cook 8 min over high heat to drive off the last of the water.
Beat the eggs with the cream, the nutmeg, the parsley, salt and pepper. Fold in the rice and the courgettes.
Pour into an oiled dish, cover with grated cheese.
Bake 35 min at 190 °C. The gratin should be set at the centre and golden at the edges.
Cook the pasta 2 min less than the stated time: it finishes in the oven and would otherwise turn to mush.
Fry the sliced mushrooms 6 min over high heat, then set them aside.
Make the béchamel: melted butter, flour, 2 min of cooking, then the hot milk poured in slowly while whisking. Let it thicken 5 min.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg, then stir in half the grated cheese off the heat.
Mix the pasta, the ham in strips, the mushrooms and the béchamel, pour into a buttered dish.
Cover with the remaining cheese and bake 20 min at 200 °C, finishing 3 min under the grill.
Split the leeks in four lengthways and rinse them under water: the grit hides between the leaves.
Slice them and melt them 20 min covered with the butter and two spoonfuls of water, over low heat.
Fry the bacon lardons 5 min in a dry pan, drain them.
Heat the oven to 190 °C, roll the pastry into the tin and prick it with a fork.
Beat the eggs with the cream, the salt, the pepper and the nutmeg.
Spread the leeks and lardons over the pastry, pour in the custard, cover with grated cheese and bake 35 min.
Heat the oven as hot as it goes, 250 °C if possible, with the tray inside: a tarte flambée is won on the heat from below.
Mix the fromage blanc and the cream, season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Slice the onions very finely and fry the bacon lardons 3 min in a dry pan.
Roll the dough out as thinly as you can on baking paper, in a rectangle.
Cover it with a thin layer of the creamy mixture, then scatter with onions and lardons.
Bake 12 min on the searing tray, until the edges are brown and crisp. Serve cut into squares, straight away.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons — the only real work in this recipe.
Stew them 45 min over very low heat in the oil, covered, with the thyme, the garlic and the sugar. They should turn golden and soft without ever colouring hard.
Uncover for 10 min to drive off the remaining juice, then salt lightly.
Heat the oven to 220 °C and roll the dough out on a tray.
Spread the stewed onions over it, lay the anchovies in a lattice and an olive in each diamond.
Bake 20 min. Best eaten warm rather than piping hot.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Slice the tomatoes 5 mm thick, salt them and let them drain 15 min on kitchen paper.
Roll the pastry into the tin, prick it all over with a fork.
Spread the base with mustard, then scatter with half the grated cheese: that layer is what shields the pastry from the juice.
Lay the tomato slices out in a rosette, packed tight — they shrink a lot.
Salt, pepper, scatter with herbes de Provence, the rest of the cheese and a drizzle of oil.
Bake 30 min, until the edges are well risen and golden.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Butter a soufflé dish with vertical brush strokes: the soufflé climbs along the streaks.
Make a roux with the butter and the flour, then pour in the hot milk, whisking. Let it thicken 5 min — it's a tight béchamel.
Off the heat, stir in the grated comté, the nutmeg, the salt and the pepper, then the egg yolks one at a time.
Whisk the whites to firm peaks with a pinch of salt.
Beat a third of them in briskly to loosen the mixture, then fold in the rest gently with a spatula, lifting the mass.
Pour into the dish, bake 30 min without ever opening the door, and serve within the minute.
Mix the buckwheat flour, 1 teaspoon of salt, an egg and 60 cl of water. Whisk to a smooth, loose batter.
Rest the batter 30 min: without a rest, the galette tears at the first touch of the spatula.
Heat a large pan, butter it lightly, pour in a ladle of batter and spread it by tilting the pan. Cook 2 min.
Turn the galette over, break an egg in the centre, lay the ham and the grated comté around it.
Fold the four sides in to make a square, carry on 3 min covered to melt the cheese while keeping the yolk runny.
Repeat for the other galettes and serve with the dressed salad.
Cook the potatoes in their skins 25 min in salted water.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Take the camembert out of its wrapping and put it back in its wooden box, without the lid.
Score the top in a criss-cross, slide slivers of garlic into the cuts.
Drizzle with honey, scatter with thyme, pepper.
Bake 20 min: the centre should be completely molten when you push a spoon in.
Serve in the middle of the table with the potatoes, the sliced baguette and the salad.
Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a loaf tin with baking paper.
Beat the eggs, add the oil and the warm milk, then the flour mixed with the baking powder. Stop working the batter as soon as it comes together.
Dice the ham, drain the olives and dry them: their brine would make the loaf sink.
Fold in ham, olives and grated cheese with a spatula, pepper generously, salt barely.
Pour into the tin and bake 45 min. A knife blade should come out dry.
Turn out while warm and cool on a rack before slicing.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and start the pasta.
Fry the bacon lardons 6 min over medium heat in a drizzle of oil, until golden and crisp.
Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan and plenty of black pepper: that is the whole sauce, there is no cream.
Take out a ladle of cooking water before draining the pasta.
Off the heat, tip the piping-hot pasta onto the lardons, add the egg and parmesan mixture and stir constantly: the heat of the pasta is enough to bind it, the pan on the flame would make an omelette.
Loosen with a little cooking water until the sauce coats, and serve immediately.
Chop carrot, onion and celery very finely, and melt them 10 min in the oil over low heat.
Add the meat, break it up with a spoon and colour it 8 min over high heat — it should brown, not boil in its juices.
Add the garlic and the tomato purée, stir 1 min.
Deglaze with red wine, let it evaporate 3 min, then pour in the milk and let it be absorbed 5 min: that is what softens the acidity of the sauce.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the herbs, salt, pepper, and simmer 1 h uncovered, over the barest heat.
Cook the pasta al dente, fold it into the sauce in the pan with a ladle of cooking water, and serve with the parmesan.
Cook the eggs 9 min in boiling water, then cool them straight away under cold water to stop the cooking and make them easier to peel.
Cook the green beans 8 min in salted water, refresh them so they keep their colour.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges, the bell pepper into thin strips, the red onion into very thin rounds.
Make the dressing: vinegar, salt, pepper, then the oil whisked in.
Lay the salad over the bottom of the dish, then the vegetables in separate piles, the flaked tuna, the eggs in quarters, the olives and the anchovies.
Pour over the dressing at the last moment and scatter with hand-torn basil.
Heat the oven grill. Cut the baguette into eight thick slices.
Slice the goat cheese log into eight rounds and lay one on each slice of bread.
Drizzle each toast with a little honey and pepper it.
Grill 5 min, until the cheese is golden and blistered — keep an eye on it, it goes from golden to black very fast.
Whisk the mustard, the vinegar, the salt and the oil, and dress the salad, the halved cherry tomatoes and the crushed walnuts with it.
Set two searing-hot toasts on each plate and serve without waiting.
Fry the bacon lardons 6 min in a dry pan, add the diced baguette to the rendered fat and brown it 3 min. Set aside.
Deglaze the pan with 2 spoonfuls of vinegar, scrape up the juices and keep that liquid.
Bring a pan of water with the rest of the vinegar to a bare simmer.
Break each egg into a bowl, slide it into the simmering water and poach 3 min, until the white is set around a yolk that is still liquid.
Whisk the mustard, the chopped shallot, the pan juices and the oil for the dressing.
Plate the dressed salad, the lardons, the croutons rubbed with garlic, and set a poached egg on each plate. Pepper.
Peel the celeriac with a knife: a peeler slips on its uneven skin.
Grate it into thick strands and pour the lemon juice over at once, or it turns black within minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise, the mustard and the crème fraîche, salt and pepper.
Fold the grated celeriac into the sauce and mix well.
Rest 10 min in the fridge before serving: the celeriac softens. Scatter with parsley.
Plump the raisins 10 min in a bowl of warm water.
Peel and grate the carrots, on the coarse side so they stay crunchy.
Squeeze the orange and the lemon, whisk the juice with the honey, the salt, the pepper and the oil.
Mix carrots, drained raisins and dressing.
Rest 10 min in the fridge and scatter with parsley just before serving.
Cook the eggs 9 min in boiling water, cool them and chop them finely.
Clean the leeks, keep only the white and a little tender green, and tie them into a bundle so they hold their shape.
Cook them 18 min in boiling salted water: a knife tip should go in without effort.
Drain them and press them gently between two plates, then let them cool to lukewarm — a wet leek waters down the dressing.
Whisk the mustard, the vinegar, the salt and the pepper, then the oil in a thin stream, and add the chopped shallot.
Spoon over the warm leeks, scatter with chopped egg and parsley.
Cook the eggs 10 min in boiling water, then plunge them into iced water: they peel without tearing the white.
Cut them in half lengthways and lift out the yolks.
Mash five yolks with a fork with the mayonnaise, the mustard, a squeeze of lemon, salt and pepper. Keep the sixth for the top.
Fill the whites with this mixture using a teaspoon, or a piping bag to make it pretty.
Crumble the remaining yolk over the top, scatter with chives and a touch of paprika, and serve on a bed of salad.
Put the salmon in the freezer for 15 min: really cold, it cuts cleanly instead of squashing.
Take off the skin and the bones, then cut it into 5 mm cubes with a knife — never in a blender.
Mix the salmon with the chopped shallot, the chives, the juice of one lime, the soy sauce, the oil, salt and pepper.
Dice the avocados and squeeze the second lime over them.
Plate in a ring, a layer of avocado then a layer of salmon, and chill 10 min.
Serve with the toasted sourdough bread.
Mix the mayonnaise, the ketchup, a few drops of lemon juice, salt and pepper: that's the cocktail sauce.
Peel the prawns and cut them in half if they are large.
Halve the avocados, take out the stone and squeeze lemon over the flesh at once.
Fold the prawns into the sauce and fill the avocado halves with it.
Scatter with chives and serve well chilled on a few salad leaves.
Slice the onions into thin slivers.
Melt them 30 min over low heat in the butter with the sugar, stirring now and then: they should turn golden brown — that is all the colour and all the flavour of the soup.
Dust with flour, stir 2 min, then deglaze with white wine.
Add 1.2 l of water, the stock cubes and the thyme, and simmer 20 min.
Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, lay two slices of toasted baguette on each and cover with grated comté.
Grill 5 min, until the cheese forms a golden crust.
Split and wash the leeks, slice them into rounds, white and tender green alike.
Sweat them 8 min in butter with the sliced onion, without colouring.
Add the diced potatoes, cover with 1 l of water and add the stock.
Cook 25 min covered, until the potatoes crush under a spoon.
Blend, add the cream, check salt and pepper.
Serve with the chopped chives. One extra potato blended in instead of a ladle of water, and the soup turns velvety.
Wash the squash and cut it into large cubes without peeling it: the skin turns tender as it cooks and gives the velouté its colour.
Fry the sliced onion and carrot 6 min in the oil.
Add the squash, cover with water, add the stock and cook 25 min covered.
Blend at length, until the velouté is perfectly smooth.
Add the cream and the nutmeg, check the seasoning.
Serve with the walnuts, crushed and toasted 2 min in a pan.
Peel and cut all the vegetables into even 2 cm pieces — even, they finish cooking together.
Sweat the onion and the leek 8 min in the oil at the bottom of a large stockpot.
Add the root vegetables, cover with 1.5 l of water, add the stock cubes.
Cook 30 min at a gentle bubble, adding the courgette after 15 min.
Blend it all for a velouté, half of it to keep some bite, or not at all.
Check the seasoning and scatter with parsley.
Rinse the lentils and cook them 25 min in three times their volume of cold water with the bouquet garni and the whole carrot. Salt only at the end.
Cook the eggs 9 min in boiling water and cool them.
Whisk the mustard, the vinegar, the salt and the pepper, then the oil in a thin stream.
Drain the lentils while still hot and tip them into the dressing: warm, they drink it up; cold, they leave it at the bottom of the bowl.
Add the chopped shallots, the cooked carrot cut into dice and the parsley.
Serve warm or cold, with the eggs in quarters.
Tip the couscous into a bowl with the lemon juice, the oil and 20 cl of cold water.
Let it swell 15 min covered, forking it through twice — that is what stops it setting into blocks.
Deseed the tomatoes and the cucumber, dice them small and add them to the couscous.
Roughly chop the mint, the parsley and the spring onions, and fold them in.
Salt, pepper, adjust the lemon, and chill 1 h before serving.
Melt the butter and let it cool to lukewarm.
Tip the flour into a bowl, make a well, break the eggs into it and whisk out from the centre.
Add the milk little by little: poured in all at once, it makes lumps that nothing can rescue.
Stir in the melted butter, the sugar, the vanilla sugar and the salt, then rest the batter 30 min.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat, barely grease it, pour in a small ladle and tilt the pan to spread it.
Cook 1 min, turn as soon as the edges lift and carry on 30 seconds. Serve with sugar and lemon juice.
Heat the oven to 180 °C and butter a round cake tin.
Tip the yoghurt into a bowl and keep the empty pot: it is the measure when you have no scales.
Add the sugar and the eggs, whisk until the mixture pales.
Stir in the oil, the vanilla, then the flour mixed with the baking powder and the salt. Stop as soon as the batter is smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake 35 min. A knife blade should come out dry.
Turn out while warm onto a rack so the base doesn't go soggy.
Melt the chocolate, broken into pieces, with the butter over a bain-marie, stirring until perfectly smooth.
Separate the whites from the yolks. Stir the yolks one at a time into the warm chocolate — if it is too hot, they cook.
Whisk the whites with the salt, showering in the sugar as they start to foam, until they hold a firm peak.
Beat a third of the whites in briskly to loosen the chocolate.
Fold in the rest in three goes, with a spatula, lifting the mass from the bottom up: mix as little as possible to keep the air.
Divide into glasses and chill at least 3 h to set.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Butter a tin and dust it with cocoa rather than flour.
Melt the chocolate and the butter over a bain-marie, then let it cool 5 min.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar and the salt until the mixture doubles in volume, 3 min.
Pour in the melted chocolate, mix, then fold in the sifted flour.
Bake 18 min exactly: the centre should still wobble slightly when you shake the tin. Two minutes more and it's a cake, not a fondant.
Rest 10 min before turning out.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Roll the pastry into the tin and prick it with a fork.
Dust the base with a spoonful of flour mixed with a little sugar: it will soak up the juice from the apples.
Peel four apples, cut them into pieces and cook them 10 min covered with 20 g of butter and the vanilla sugar, then crush them to a compote.
Spread the compote over the pastry base.
Slice the two remaining apples thinly and lay them in a tight rosette, dust with sugar and cinnamon, dot with the remaining butter.
Bake 35 min, then glaze with warm honey as it comes out of the oven.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Peel the apples and cut them into large cubes.
Toss them with the lemon juice and the cinnamon, then spread them in a gratin dish.
With your fingertips, rub the flour, the cold diced butter, the brown sugar and the salt into large uneven crumbs. The butter must stay cold, or the mixture turns into a cream.
Add the flaked almonds to the crumbs and cover the apples with them, without pressing down.
Bake 35 min, until the top is golden and the juice bubbles at the edges.
Let it cool 10 min before serving.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Butter a dish and dust it with a spoonful of sugar.
Wash the cherries and pull off the stalks. Leave the stones in: they perfume the batter as it bakes, but warn your guests.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, the vanilla sugar and the salt, then fold in the flour.
Loosen with the milk poured in slowly, until the batter is as fluid as a crêpe batter.
Scatter the cherries in the dish, pour the batter over them.
Bake 40 min, until the clafoutis is puffed and golden. Eaten warm.
Blanch the rice 3 min in boiling water then drain it: that removes the excess surface starch and stops it catching.
Bring the milk to a bare simmer with the vanilla, the salt and the butter.
Tip the rice in and cook 35 min over very low heat, stirring regularly — the stirring is what makes rice pudding creamy.
Add the sugar only halfway through: added too early, it hardens the grain.
Off the heat, stir in the cream. The mixture should stay loose, it thickens as it cools.
Serve warm or cold, in pots.
Separate the whites from the yolks. Heat the milk with the vanilla without letting it boil.
Whisk the yolks with 80 g of sugar until they pale.

Pour the hot milk over them, whisking, return to low heat and stir with a spatula 8 min: the custard is ready when it coats the spoon and a finger drawn through leaves a clean line. It must never boil.
Strain the custard and chill it.
Whisk the whites to firm peaks with the salt and 40 g of sugar, then poach them in large spoonfuls 2 min in simmering milk, turning them halfway.
Make a golden caramel with the remaining sugar and a little water. Set the whites on the custard, pour over the caramel and scatter with toasted almonds.
Heat the oven to 100 °C. Heat the cream and the milk with the vanilla, without boiling, then let it infuse 10 min.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar, without frothing: bubbles would leave a foam on the surface of the ramekins.
Pour the hot mixture over the yolks, stirring, then pass it through a fine sieve.
Divide between six shallow ramekins and bake 50 min. The custard should be set at the edges and still wobbly in the middle.
Cool then chill at least 3 h.
Just before serving, dust with brown sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch or 3 min under a searing grill.
Soak the prunes 20 min in warm water, then drain them.
Heat the oven to 200 °C and generously butter a deep-sided dish.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, the vanilla sugar and the salt, add the flour then the milk in a thin stream until the batter is smooth and runny.
Stir in the melted butter, pour the batter into the dish and scatter in the prunes.
Bake 15 min at 200 °C, then drop to 180 °C and carry on 35 min.
The far should be golden, almost brown in places. Eaten warm or cold, never hot.
Use stale bread: fresh, it soaks through too fast and falls apart in the pan.
Beat the eggs with the milk, half the sugar and the vanilla sugar in a shallow dish.
Dip each slice 20 seconds a side, no more.
Foam the butter in a pan over medium heat and brown the slices 3 min on each side.
Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon and dust it over the slices while still hot.
Melt the butter and let it cool to lukewarm.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, the honey, the lemon zest and the salt until the mixture is foamy, 3 min.
Fold in the flour sifted with the baking powder, then the melted butter.
Chill the batter at least 1 h: the shock between cold batter and hot oven is what makes the hump.
Heat the oven to 220 °C, fill the moulds two thirds full.
Bake 4 min at 220 °C then drop to 180 °C and carry on 6 min. Turn out at once.
Heat the oven to 170 °C and line a loaf tin.
Weigh the eggs: that weight gives you the weight of the butter, the sugar and the flour. That is the whole principle of the cake.
Beat the soft butter with the sugar to a pale cream, 4 min with a whisk.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking well between each, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour sifted with the baking powder and the salt, with a spatula and without labouring it.
Pour into the tin and bake 50 min. Cool before slicing — a quatre-quarts is better the next day.
Heat the oven to 190 °C. Roll out the pastry, prick it, cover it with weighted paper and blind bake 20 min, until golden.
Squeeze the lemons and zest two of them.
Whisk 3 whole eggs and 3 yolks with 150 g of sugar and the cornflour, then add the juice and the zest.
Cook this mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, 6 min, until it thickens, then beat in the butter off the heat.
Pour the curd onto the cooled base and let it set 1 h in the fridge.
Whisk the 3 remaining whites to peaks with the salt, tighten with the remaining 100 g of sugar until the meringue is smooth and glossy.
Cover the tart with meringue, pulling it into peaks, dust with icing sugar and grill 5 min, keeping an eye on it.
Start the jasmine rice.
Heat the thick part of the coconut milk 3 min in a wok, until the oil separates and glistens on the surface.
Fry the curry paste in it 2 min, crushing it with the spatula: this step is what wakes the spices up, skipping it gives a flat curry.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add the crushed kaffir lime leaves, the fish sauce and the palm sugar.
Add the green beans in lengths and the bell pepper in strips, simmer 6 min.
Tip in the prawns and cook 3 min, no more: beyond that they turn rubbery.
Off the heat, add the Thai basil and a squeeze of lime. Serve with the rice.
Brown the chicken pieces 8 min in the wok, then set them aside.
Fry the massaman paste 2 min in the thick part of the coconut milk, until it smells fragrant.
Return the chicken, pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add the cinnamon and bring to a simmer.
Add the potatoes in large cubes and the onions in wedges, cover and simmer 30 min.
Season with the fish sauce, the palm sugar and the tamarind — a massaman stands on the balance of salt, sweet and sour, adjusted by the spoonful.
Add the peanuts, carry on 5 min and serve with the jasmine rice.
Peel the prawns, keeping the heads and shells.
Fry the shells 3 min in a dry pan, cover with 1.2 l of water and simmer 15 min, then strain: this broth is the whole difference from a soup made with water.
Crush the lemongrass stalks with the flat of a knife and cut them into lengths. Slice the galangal into rounds.
Add to the broth the lemongrass, the galangal, the crushed kaffir lime leaves, the crushed shallots and the curry paste. Let it infuse 5 min.
Add the mushrooms and the cherry tomatoes, cook 3 min, then the prawns, 2 min.
Off the heat: fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, crushed chillies and coriander. Never let it boil after the lime, it would lose its perfume.
Bring 50 cl of water to a simmer with the stock, the sliced galangal, the crushed lemongrass and the kaffir lime leaves. Let it infuse 10 min.
Pour in the coconut milk and hold it just below boiling — boiled, coconut splits and goes grainy.
Add the finely sliced chicken and the mushrooms, cook 8 min.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar.
Off the heat, add the lime juice, the crushed chillies and the coriander.
Serve as it is or with a bowl of rice: the lemongrass stalks and the galangal are left at the side of the plate.
Peel the green papaya and grate it into long strands on the coarse side, or cut it into fine strips with a knife. Do the same with the carrot.
Pound the garlic and the chillies in a mortar, coarsely.
Add the palm sugar, the fish sauce and the lime juice, pound until the sugar dissolves.
Add the green beans cut into lengths and the cherry tomatoes, crush them lightly so they release their juice.
Add the papaya and the carrot, mixing by pounding gently with one hand and stirring with the other: you bruise the fibres so they drink the dressing, you don't purée them.
Scatter with crushed peanuts and serve immediately, before the papaya gives up its water.
Toast the 2 spoonfuls of jasmine rice in a dry pan 5 min, until golden brown, then grind it to a coarse powder in a mortar. That is what gives larb its texture and its nutty perfume.
Cook the minced chicken 6 min in a pan with 3 spoonfuls of water, pressing it with the spatula so it stays in grains. No fat: larb is not a stir-fry.
Off the heat, let it cool 2 min then add the fish sauce, the lime juice, the sugar and the dried chilli.
Add the sliced shallots, the spring onions and the toasted rice powder.
Fold in the chopped mint and coriander at the last moment.
Serve warm with the salad leaves and the cucumber batons, to pick the larb up by hand.

pad-krapow-porc.titre: Pad krapow, pork with Thai basil
etapes: Start the jasmine rice.
Pound the garlic and the chillies together in a mortar, to a rough paste.
Heat the wok until searing with a spoonful of oil, throw in the garlic and chilli paste for 20 seconds.
Add the pork and sear it 4 min over maximum heat, pressing it with the spatula.
Add the green beans in short lengths, the oyster sauce, the soy sauce, the fish sauce and the sugar, stir-fry 2 min.
Cut the heat and throw in the Thai basil: the residual heat is enough to wilt it, cooked it loses everything.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the very hot oil, lacy edges and runny yolk, and set one on each plate of rice.
Soak the wide rice noodles as their packet says, until supple but still firm. Drain them and oil them lightly so they don't stick.
Slice the chicken into strips and toss it with a spoonful of soy sauce.
Heat the wok very hard, sear the chicken 3 min, then push it to the side.
Break the eggs into the middle, scramble them 30 seconds, add the garlic and the chinese cabbage cut into lengths, stir-fry 2 min.
Add the noodles, the sauces and the sugar. Stir-fry 3 min, flipping with the spatula rather than stirring in circles: the noodles should pick up charred marks, the signature of the dish.
Pepper generously and serve with the rice vinegar on the side.
Cook the rice the day before if you can and let it cool in the fridge: warm, damp rice turns to mush in the wok.
Heat the wok over maximum heat, sear the diced chicken 4 min, then the garlic and the onion 1 min.
Push to one side, break in the eggs and scramble them quickly.
Add the cold rice, breaking up the grains by hand, stir-fry 3 min, pressing the grains against the side of the wok.
Season with fish sauce, soy sauce and sugar, add the tomatoes in wedges and the spring onions, stir-fry 1 min.
Serve with the cucumber in rounds and a lime wedge to squeeze over.
Cut the chicken into long strips and toss them with half the coconut milk, the turmeric, the ground coriander and a spoonful of fish sauce. Marinate 20 min.
Start the jasmine rice.
For the sauce: fry the curry paste 2 min in a little oil, add the rest of the coconut milk, the blitzed peanuts, the sugar and the remaining fish sauce.
Let it thicken 8 min over low heat, stirring: the sauce should coat, loosen it with a little water if it tightens too much.
Thread the strips onto skewers and grill them 3 min a side in a pan or on the barbecue, until the edges caramelise.
Serve with the peanut sauce, the cucumber in rounds and the limes.

curry-jaune-poulet.titre: Yellow curry with chicken and potatoes
etapes: Fry the yellow curry paste and the turmeric 2 min in the hot oil, until the aroma rises.
Add the chicken pieces and coat them 3 min.
Pour in the coconut milk and 20 cl of water, bring to a simmer.
Add the potatoes in cubes, the carrots in rounds and the onion in wedges.
Simmer 30 min covered, until the potatoes are meltingly soft.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, add the lime and the coriander off the heat. Serve with the rice.

yam-woon-sen.titre: Yam woon sen, glass noodle salad
etapes: Soak the glass noodles 8 min in hot water, then drain them and cut them with scissors into manageable lengths.
Poach the minced pork 3 min in a pan of simmering water, breaking it up, then the prawns 2 min. Drain it all.
Make the dressing: pound the garlic and the chillies, add the fish sauce, the sugar and the lime juice.
Mix the warm noodles, the pork, the prawns, the sliced shallots, the celery in thin slices and the cherry tomatoes.
Pour over the dressing and mix by hand: warm, the noodles drink it up.
Add the coriander and the spring onions, scatter with crushed peanuts and serve at once.
Start the jasmine rice. Set up a steamer basket over a pan of boiling water.
Line the basket with chinese cabbage and lengths of crushed lemongrass, lay the fish on top and score it twice across the top.
Cover and steam 12 min: the flesh should flake apart at the first touch of a fork.
Meanwhile, pound the garlic and the chillies, then slacken with the lime juice, the fish sauce, the sugar and 10 cl of hot stock.
Pour this searing sauce over the fish as it comes out of the basket.
Cover with whole sprigs of coriander, stalks included, and serve with the rice.
Start the rice.
Beat the eggs hard with a fork with the fish sauce, a squeeze of lime and the chopped spring onions, until the mixture is foamy: the beaten-in air is what makes the omelette puff.
Heat the oil in a wok until it shimmers — you need plenty, a Thai omelette is deep-fried, not pan-fried.
Pour the eggs in all at once, from a height: they should blister at the edges immediately.
Cook 2 min, turn and carry on 1 min, until the omelette is golden and crisp.
Drain on kitchen paper, set on the rice, pepper and serve with the sriracha.
Start the rice. Slice the beef into thin strips across the grain — that is what keeps it tender.
Mix the oyster sauce, the soy sauce, the fish sauce and the sugar in a bowl: the stir-fry will go too fast to measure along the way.
Heat the wok until it smokes, sear the beef in two batches, 90 seconds a batch, and set it aside. Overloaded, the wok braises instead of searing.
Throw in the garlic and the chillies for 20 seconds, then the onion and the bell pepper in strips, 2 min over maximum heat.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce, stir-fry 1 min.
Cut the heat, add the Thai basil and stir once. Serve immediately.
Pound the garlic, the coriander roots and stalks, the sliced lemongrass and the pepper into a rough paste.
Mix in the fish sauce, the soy sauce, the palm sugar and the turmeric.
Coat the thighs in this marinade and chill at least 30 min, overnight if you can.
Soak the sticky rice 30 min, then steam it 25 min in a cloth.
Grill the thighs 15 min a side over medium heat, skin down first, brushing them with marinade. Over too fierce a heat, the sugar burns before the flesh is cooked.
Serve with the sticky rice, the sriracha let down with a little lime juice, and the rest of the coriander.
Start the rice. Cut every vegetable before you light the wok: once it is going, a stir-fry leaves no time to chop anything.
Drain and press the tofu, cut it into cubes and brown it 6 min on all sides. Set aside.
Slake the cornflour in 10 cl of water with the oyster sauce, the soy sauce and the sugar.
Heat the wok over maximum heat, throw in the garlic and the ginger for 20 seconds.
Add carrots and broccoli, stir-fry 3 min, then the mushrooms and the pak choi, 2 min more. The vegetables should stay crunchy.
Pour in the sauce, return the tofu, let it coat 1 min and serve over the rice.
Bring 1.5 l of water to a simmer with the stock cubes, the sliced ginger and the crushed garlic. Let it infuse 15 min.
Poach the chicken breasts 12 min in this broth, over very low heat, then lift them out and shred them by hand.
Season the broth with fish sauce, soy sauce and palm sugar, and strain it.
Soak the rice noodles 5 min in hot water, then dip them 30 seconds in the broth before dividing them between the bowls.
Add the shredded chicken, the bean sprouts and the searing broth.
Everyone finishes their own bowl: spring onions, coriander, crushed peanuts, dried chilli and lime.
Rinse the sticky rice until the water runs clear, then soak it at least 3 h, overnight if you can. Without soaking, it stays hard at the centre.
Steam it 25 min in a cloth, until the grains are translucent and sticky.
Heat 30 cl of coconut milk with the sugar and the salt without boiling, until dissolved.
Pour this over the hot rice, stir and let it stand 20 min covered: the rice should absorb it all.
Thicken the rest of the coconut milk with the slaked cornflour, 2 min over low heat, for the sauce to spoon over.
Plate the rice with the mango cheeks sliced, spoon over the sauce and scatter with toasted sesame.
